Unfortunately, current mechanistic modeling approaches are inadequate for robust prediction of dynamic behavior in HR-CS (Ngo 2023). Therefore, the ultimate goal of this work is to develop a data-driven tool to control the secondary treatment process to keep its ESS below 25 mg/L. 32 The Water Research Foundation This goal can be achieved through a two-step process: 1. Objective 1: Develop a data-driven model that links HR-CS operational conditions and ESS. For this model to serve the goal of controlling the process ESS, the project team subjected model development to two specific constraints: - Successfully capture ESS daily dynamics. - Be sensitive to changes in the manipulated variables (SPB and WNS flow rates). 2. Objective 2: Based on the developed model, develop a decision-making tool to inform operators with the optimal SPB and WNS flow rates to control ESS below 25 mg/L. 5.1.3 Get Data Data in this study derived from historical records (since the secondary treatment process switched to HR-CS in 2020) coupled to a 16-week dedicated data collection campaign. The time span for data collection (historical data and data collection campaign) represents 28 months (2 years and 4 months) of full-scale data from August 2020 to December 2022. For this period, more than 50 input variables were routinely collected. As shown in Figure 5-3, these variables were collected from multiple sources using different methods and with different collection frequencies. The PCS-based data are collected from online sensors and available with high frequency on a daily basis. This includes different flow rates like SPB flow rate (SPB_Q) and WNS flow rate (WNS_Q), dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration via online sensors, and mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) probe data.
